reasoning: An active positive radius implies Ru>0 and sLower<sUpperRaw, so the radius projection gives the complete nonempty admissible s interval.
The two endpoint inequalities F(sLower,Z)<Tu and F(sUpper,Z)>max(0,Tl) give exactly the stated strict lower and upper bounds for Z squared.
The upper bound gives Z squared<2^(1-2h). On 1/2<=s<=2 this implies dF/ds>1-8h>1/2, so endpoint inequalities are sufficient for a unique admissible root.

Intersecting the open axial box with the negative and positive intervals preserves an open intersection; when the lower squared bound is negative, omitting the single point Z=0 cannot remove that intersection.
Negative-first chooses one nonempty open interval and its midpoint. The time midpoint then yields a unique root strictly within the admissible s interval.
The final radius midpoint lies strictly in both the mesh radius interval and the original annular shell.
All three coordinate differences within one open mesh box are<3/(2*ell^6), so Euclidean distance<3*sqrt(3)/(2*ell^6)<4/ell^6=4/S^3.
The representative depends on the fixed label and original constants, not the current source point or residual. Its slow derivatives are zero.
